stem: A 58-year-old man with long-standing hepatitis-B cirrhosis develops right-upper-quadrant pain, weight loss and rapidly worsening ascites, with a markedly raised serum alpha-fetoprotein. Triple-phase CT shows a mass with arterial-phase enhancement and venous-phase 'washout'. The most likely diagnosis is:
concept: Hepatocellular carcinoma arises on a background of cirrhosis (HBV, HCV, alcohol, aflatoxin); the clues are a rising AFP and the classic arterial enhancement with venous 'washout' on triple-phase imaging. A haemangioma shows peripheral nodular enhancement with a normal AFP.
subject: Pathology
